properties.title: Sonata: A Hybrid World Model for Inertial Kinematics under Clinical Data Scarcity

membership.reason: Sonata is a JEPA-style latent-predictive kinematic world model (linear Koopman predictor + SIGReg + Gated DeltaNet recurrent state) predicting future trunk IMU latent state.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L0 latent-predictive representation world model (WT_PHYSIOLOGY, BP_COMPONENT).

properties.backbone: 3.77M-param [C,C,C,G]x3 hybrid (gated long convolutions + Gated DeltaNet) + linear Koopman latent predictor + SIGReg

properties.flow: 6-axis lumbar/waist IMU (100 Hz) -> [C,C,C,G]x3 hybrid encoder -> latent state & Koopman next-window prediction (LIN) -> frozen linear probes

properties.purpose: Wearable inertial kinematic representation learning for neurological gait assessment and fall-risk stratification.
properties.environment: 9 public clinical/activity IMU cohorts + OOD PAMAP2 probe

assertions.rationale: Harmonized 9 public 6-axis trunk/waist IMU datasets resampled to 100 Hz with gravity retained.
3.77M-parameter [C,C,G]x3 hybrid encoder interleaving gated long convolutions with Gated DeltaNet.
LIN pretraining head predicts future window latent state via projector + linear Koopman predictor.
SIGReg variance-covariance/isotropic regularization prevents latent collapse.
Associative recurrent state S_t updated via gated delta rule.
Learned [C,C,G]x3 backbone with linear Koopman latent predictor.
On-device wearable inference for neurological gait and fall-risk representation learning.
Decoder probe Val MAE (0.00260) and UCI HAR forecast MAE @ h=48 (0.02131).
Cross-cohort transfer (SisFall SA->SE AUC 0.963), AWGN noise robustness (@10 dB), and OOD PAMAP2 transfer.
Compact 3.77M parameter budget compatible with on-device wearable inference.
Predicts future kinematic state in compact latent space rather than raw sensor space.

evidence_fragments.content: Sonata is a 3.77M-parameter hybrid model, pretrained on a harmonised corpus of nine public datasets (∼739 subjects, ∼190k windows) with a latent world-model objective that predicts future state rather than reconstructing raw sensor traces. In a controlled comparison against a matched autoregressive forecasting baseline (MAE) on the same backbone, Sonata yields consistently stronger frozen-probe clinical discrimination, prospective fall-risk prediction, and cross-cohort transfer across a 14-arm evaluation suite, while producing higher-rank, more structured latent representations. At 3.77M parameters the model is compatible with on-device wearable inference, offering a step toward general kinematic world models for neurological assessment.

[paraphrase (visual p.5)] Table 1 lists the 9-dataset harmonized corpus (Voisard, WearGait-PD, Mobilise-D TVS, LTMM, SisFall, UCI HAR, UMAFall, FallAllD, USC-HAD; ~739 subjects, 190,495 windows). Sections 4.1-4.2 specify the 12-layer [C,C,C,G]x3 hybrid backbone interleaving gated long convolutions (rFFT) with Gated DeltaNet recurrent associative state S_t updated via the gated delta rule (Eq. 2).

[paraphrase (visual p.9)] Table 2 and Figure 3 report a controlled 14-arm comparison of LIN (projector + linear Koopman predictor + SIGReg) vs matched MAE raw-signal forecasting: WearGait-PD AUC 0.756 vs 0.631, Mobilise-D TVS AUC 0.613 vs 0.461, LTMM fall risk AUC 0.670 vs 0.621, SisFall SA->SE AUC 0.963 vs 0.874, Effective rank 59.1 vs 33.0, Dynamics H-stat 15.26 vs 12.08, Latent straightness -0.2973 vs -0.3798. Authors explicitly state modest absolute scores are comparative evidence under a difficult protocol, not evidence of clinical readiness.

passing through a 12-layer [C,C,C,G] ×3 hybrid backbone—where C denotes a Long-convolution block and G denotes a Gated DeltaNet block—terminating in a latent read-out that feeds into lightweight pretraining heads and a frozen linear probe for downstream evaluation

capability_assessments.rationale: JEPA-style latent-predictive kinematic world model (LIN Koopman predictor + SIGReg + Gated DeltaNet) evaluated via frozen downstream probes without action conditioning or multi-step observation rollouts (L0).

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R2 Multi-cohort offline & OOD representation evaluation

limitations: Unconditioned latent-predictive pretraining for frozen-probe representation learning rather than action-conditioned counterfactual rollout.
Modest absolute classification scores on heterogeneous cohorts; authors explicitly disclaim clinical readiness.
notes: All 18 physical PDF pages extracted/read; pages 1 and 5 visually inspected via rendered PNGs.

legacy_cells.FN: Under the matched-backbone 14-arm frozen-probe suite, the latent-predictive objective generally favored clinical discrimination/robustness, whereas raw-signal forecasting favored reconstruction. These mixed results do not establish universal superiority of the latent objective.
